messages:
elaine: FYI: We had ~50 toolcall traces this morning where the validator marked the response as FATAL and traffic got routed to the degen variant. Costs spiked and a few customers hit quota alerts.
priya: ugh. do we have an example trace id?
elaine: trace: abc-2026-03-20-01. here's the raw tool payload from logs:
```json
{"tool": "price_lookup", "output": "{\"price\": 12.99,\"currency\": \"USD\",}\n```
(priya: that trailing comma is the culprit — but it's only in the tool output string; the agent wrapped it into a string field so top-level JSON parsed but schema validator runs on parsed 'structured_output' and fails strict object shape)
jay: so validator sees structured_output parse -> object with an extra trailing-comma artifact? can you paste the exact error message from schema-bot?
schema-bot: [automated] validation_error: path=structured_output, rule=object-strict, reason="unexpected token after value", classification=FATAL, sample=true
priya: current behavior: any parse or schema mismatch maps to classification=FATAL and triggers the routing policy that forces degen fallback. That behavior was intentionally conservative, but it's causing noisy customer impact for small parse quirks.
sam: +1 we should avoid full traffic failover for minor formatting issues. proposal: add a SOFT_REJECT classification with a score and granular reasons so router can make policy decisions (e.g., allow passthrough with warning or short-circuit to a repair pipeline).
jay: concrete: change validator output to emit one of {OK, SOFT_REJECT, HARD_REJECT}. SOFT_REJECT includes fields: score (0..1), reasons[], sample_flag. Router policy would be configurable: org-level canary might treat score<0.6 as passthrough, 0.6-0.9 repair, >0.9 hard fallback.
priya: implementation notes: validator currently returns HTTP 400 style metadata. We'll need to add new telemetry counters: toolcall.validation.ok, toolcall.validation.soft_reject, toolcall.validation.hard_reject, plus a histogram for soft_reject.score. Also we need a deterministic sampling tag (sample=true) so we can collect payloads for debugging without logging everything.
elaine: we also need to ensure billing/quota classification doesn't flip when we soft-reject. Right now any non-OK marks the request as 'fallback' in billing which caused customers to be charged at a higher tier. Need to keep billing unit attribution stable (i.e., still count as primary model tokens unless actual routed model changes).
jay: agree. plan: separate telemetry channel for 'validation_classification' and a routing decision event. Only the routing event should affect billing. validator should NOT emit routing decisions. Router will subscribe and decide based on classification + org policy.
sam: small code sketch for validator output (pseudocode):
```json
// validator response (new schema)
{
  "status": "SOFT_REJECT",
  "score": "0.42",
  "reasons": ["trailing-comma-in-embedded-json", "nullable-field-mismatch"],
  "sample": "true",
  "example_snippet": "{\"price\": 12.99,\"currency\": \"USD\",}"
}
```
priya: router pseudo-policy:
```
if status == OK: forward to primary
elif status == SOFT_REJECT and score < 0.6: forward with warning header
elif status == SOFT_REJECT and score >= 0.6 and score < 0.9: send to repair pipeline (async) then forward primary
else: route to fallback model and emit routing_event=fallback
```
jay: rollout plan: default behavior for existing orgs stays unchanged for now. We'll enable soft-reject semantics for internal canary orgs at 1% traffic first. Add console flag in Rollouts UI to toggle: "validator.strictness: soft|strict". Also add dashboard tile showing soft_reject ratio per org and sample traces link.
priya: observability work: add metric names + tags: metric=toolcall.validation.count, tag=classification:(ok|soft|hard), tag=org, tag=model_variant. Backfill: run a 48h job to reclassify recent rejects with new logic to estimate impact.
elaine: tests: add unit tests for parser recovery (strip trailing commas, allow quoted-json heuristics) and integration test that ensures soft_reject does not change billing events.
sam: question: are we comfortable changing validator API shape? SDKs ingest validator metadata now. Breaking change risk.
jay: keep backward compatibility: if clients expect boolean ok/fail, continue to emit a legacy field "ok": true/false derived from status (ok => true, soft_reject => false) but also include new 'status' and 'score'. Deprecate legacy field via header.
priya: PRs: 1) validator: emit new schema + sampling flag + tests. 2) router: consume status/score, decouple billing emission. 3) console: add Rollouts toggle + dashboard tile. 4) backfill job + migration playbook.
elaine: owners? priya -> validator PR, jay -> router changes, sam -> console tile, i'll own the backfill and migration doc. Can we target canary by next Wednesday?
priya: building now, will have draft PR by EOD tmrw.
jay: I'll sketch router change this afternoon.
schema-bot: [automated] note: created issue INF-6723 for validator soft_reject work.
elaine: sweet. last ask: add a small log-level header when we forward with warning like `x-tool-validate: soft(score=0.42)` so downstream services can choose to surface non-fatal validation warnings in traces.
sam: +1 that will help customer support.
elaine: ok locking this thread. thanks all. action items recorded in INF-6723. :thumbsup:
